title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
abstract: arXiv:2611.18559v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future co

translated_title: BAL：基于潜空间双向自回归的人体运动表示学习方法
translated_abstract: 从3D姿态序列中学习具有语义意义的人体运动表示对于人类行为建模至关重要。现有的自监督方法从人工假设中获取监督信号，例如对一定范围内数据增强的不变性，或在特定时间尺度上被掩码区域的可恢复性，这引入了启发式超参数，使得学习到的语义对这些设置非常敏感。我们提出了BAL，一种自监督框架，它转而利用人体运动内在的监督信号：日常行为的自然顺序结构。BAL在语义抽象的潜空间中进行自回归预测，这类似于人类在预测他人行为时关注的是动作本身而非精确的关节配置。时间上的前向与后向双向自回归预测充分挖掘了这些顺序约束，同时使得模型能够利用过去和未来的上下文来提取表示。
tldr: 本文提出BAL自监督框架，利用人体日常行为的自然时间顺序作为内在监督信号，通过潜空间中的双向自回归预测学习人体运动表示，避免了以往人工假设引入的启发式超参数问题。
en_tdlr: BAL is a self-supervised framework that learns human movement representations by exploiting the intrinsic natural ordering of everyday behavior through bidirectional autoregressive prediction in a semantically abstract latent space.
